findings.rationale: The retained rebuilt wheel and shipped wheel are byte-identical at SHA-256 882b2f9d13fb16a2a756c21e73d3758789c1f5084129cdef3ae349ca4c8cb773, but their milai payload contains four files absent from current-source: milai/py.typed, milai/static/milai.css, milai/static/milai.js, and milai/templates/index.html. The wheel has 65 milai payload files while current-source/runtime/src/milai has 61, with exactly those four missing. The build configuration packages src/milai, Flask explicitly uses the missing static/templates directories, and the UI route renders the missing index.html. The closure builder only inventories runtime/src/**/*.py, so it silently excludes package-data inputs. Neither the 379-entry runner/helper closure nor the 418-entry source inventory contains these assets. Therefore the claimed independent rebuild was performed from a richer, unmaterialized filesystem state and cannot be reproduced from the closed candidate bytes. This leaves the parent R2 hermeticity finding open despite the valid captures and BFCL tracked-tree remediation.

parent_finding_closures.rationale: Bootstrap authority is derived only from the fixed imported dual-AI aggregate, active identities, source replay, and stage ledger. Release remains hard-disabled and caller-authored success mappings cannot authorize it.

The active importer validates immutable raw xhigh event streams, processes, outputs, bundle identity, all 24 parent closures, and two agreeing distinct primary threads before minting receipts. The legacy bootstrap importer cannot mint accepted stages.
AI stage acceptance and model-call authority are separate. Accepted R0-R2 receipts can derive only the exact 24-slot bootstrap capability; they do not directly permit a call, test access, or release.

Claim admission now requires an ACCEPTED stage, AI-independent gate receipts with exact internal gate/stage/candidate/source semantics, the active inventory root, verified evidence hashes, and an allowed claim. Aggregate claims, test access, and release remain denied.

The call ledger has exact typed states, a contiguous hash chain, fsync-backed append transitions, unique attempts and native IDs, pre-I/O provider claims, raw-response binding, terminal reconciliation, and fail-closed handling of missing or incomplete states.

The upstream BFCL remediation is valid, but R2 is still non-hermetic: four execution-relevant package-data inputs present in the retained wheel are absent from current-source and both active source closures. The wheel cannot be independently rebuilt from the bundle.

The fixed bootstrap executor is the sole pre-R3 completion path. Every enumerated non-bootstrap production completion literal is protected by replay of an active accepted R3 artifact, including the host-derived OpenWorker capability boundary.

Quality authorization binds exact disjoint 50+50 case manifests, required knowledge-update and temporal strata, the exact attempt ledger, and a fixed dual-xhigh approval. Full-test execution additionally requires atomic one-use capability consumption.

The fixed 216-case manifest binds exact 80 multi-turn, 122 supported-single-turn, and 24 irrelevance denominators to one coherent worker/environment/adapter/upstream identity frozen before manifest freeze. The scorer fixes these paths, requires result access after freeze, and exactly reconciles every per-case attempt to the append-only ledger.

Serving gates rebuild attempts and aggregate cells only from a fixed workload, fixed raw-receipt set, fixed attempt ledger, and fixed cell-window receipt. Raw receipts must exactly cover the ledger and bind native IDs, usage, terminal state, timing, workload, and global uniqueness. Zero active digests keep serving fail-closed until raw artifacts exist.

The audit contract truthfully requires AI_INDEPENDENT_PER_USER_POLICY, gpt-5.6-sol, xhigh, primary role, explicit boundary declarations, exact stage decisions, findings, and no human-authority representation; the importer validates those semantics.

The materialized active ledger is a six-entry, monotonic, append-only hash chain with one AUTHOR_CANDIDATE and one REVIEW_REQUIRED transition for each R0-R2 stage. The checkpoint exactly binds all 4276 bytes, six entries, terminal chain hash, source root, and current states.

The importer and authorization gate use fixed immutable aggregate, raw process/event/output, policy, identity, source, and ledger paths; caller-supplied stage receipts cannot confer bootstrap or release authority.

Protected test access requires the fixed immutable dual-xhigh test-access bundle and active identities, followed by atomic one-use capability consumption. A hand-authored approval mapping is insufficient.

Authorization derives exactly 24 fixed slot IDs once from the accepted aggregate and active ledger. The executor fixes the ledger/capability paths, creates the ledger exclusively, enforces the exact slot set, and the adapter replays authority before every native request.

The specifically missing migrations/script.py.mako byte is now materialized and appears with the same digest in the active runner/helper closure and complete candidate source inventory. The separate package-data omission is tracked under DG10-C3-AI-006.
The immutable reasoning amendment and active acceptance/validator consistently require gpt-5.6-sol with xhigh. The interrupted max process has no review or authorization effect.

The rebuilt wheel bytes are retained, manifest-bound, and byte-identical to the shipped content-addressed wheel at SHA-256 882b2f9d13fb16a2a756c21e73d3758789c1f5084129cdef3ae349ca4c8cb773. This closes retention of rebuild output, although source completeness remains open separately.

The full-test callback boundary atomically consumes its fixed capability before invoking the callback and revalidates the consumed state afterward; replay, replacement, or non-consumption fails closed.
Collection, pytest, and Ruff commands all explicitly select the same manifest-bound evals/dg10/pyproject.toml. Captures show 253 collected and passed tests and a successful Ruff check.

The adapter durably and atomically claims a fixed planned slot and fsyncs PROVIDER_CLAIMED before opening the network request. Direct, repeated, and concurrent reuse is rejected before network I/O; raw response and native ID are journaled before semantic validation.

The successor sequence is temporally coherent: execution identity freeze precedes case-manifest freeze, both precede dependent R0-R2 ledger transitions, ledger timestamps are monotonic, and the fixed scorer rejects result access at or before manifest freeze. The active identity succession records zero target completion calls and no test access before supersession.

The active R1 validation uses scope all, embeds the complete 418-entry inventory rooted at de82b2ac23b269c89cac9a5707f14114d099df47bb89d98e9501fef070db69ce, and is the sole subordinate receipt in the R1 author binding. Ledger reconciliation explicitly compares that subordinate internal root to the ledger root.

The frozen completion-boundary test enumerates every production completion literal. The fixed 24-slot executor is the only pre-R3 route; local vLLM, OpenWorker, serving, BFCL, smoke, and judge clients require either that sealed adapter or an active accepted R3 gate.
